2df6dde2e7.q: What is the white-glove advisor approach to dental practice transitions as practiced by Triumph and Transition Partners?
2df6dde2e7.a: The white-glove approach means asking doctors what they need, what they're looking to accomplish, and what can improve their quality of life and set them up for the future. Instead of a shotgun approach with multiple bidders, Nate Thompson focuses on deeply listening to understand each seller's priorities—whether scaling properly, avoiding lender delays, or finding true alignment in values. The firm represents sellers only, ensuring their best interests are protected and post-sale regret is minimized by matching them thoughtfully with one right partner rather than competing options.

1a343417d8.q: How did Nate Thompson discover Innovate32 as the right partner for Dr. Dwight Poron's Fort Bend Dental group?
1a343417d8.a: Nate listened deeply to Dwight's vision of building a Mayo Clinic-style comprehensive care model for dentistry rather than competing on growth metrics alone. After multiple conversations, Nate identified Josh Johnson, who had been brought in as CEO to start what later became Innovate32, as the one person who aligned with Dwight's thesis on patient care and comprehensive quality as a core KPI. Nate matched them not through a shotgun approach but by critically thinking about who would fit best with Dwight's mission and values.

ad66e7b44f.q: Why did Nate Thompson reject the traditional multi-bidder approach common among dental practice brokers?
ad66e7b44f.a: Nate realized that when multiple strategic partners compete to acquire a practice, it often leads to post-sale regret because the highest bidder typically isn't the right cultural or mission fit. Instead of farming practices out to 20 competitors, he built Triumph and Transition Partners on a seller-only representation model to ensure doctors are truly fired up about their partnership and that alignment on patient care, values, and long-term goals takes priority over maximizing valuation alone.

10d765db9b.q: What made Dwight Poron interested in seeking a strategic partner despite Fort Bend Dental's success?
10d765db9b.a: Although Fort Bend Dental was thriving and growing, Dwight realized that all the growth remained on his shoulders and his family's shoulders from a personal guarantee standpoint. As debt increased, traditional bank lending options became limited. He wanted to continue the entrepreneurial drive to serve a greater portion of the population beyond Houston while not bearing all the risk alone, which made him open to finding the right partner who shared his comprehensive care philosophy.
